title: A 20 year vertical of Kumeu River’s Hunting Hill Chardonnay
summary: Website: https://kumeuriver.co.nz/ As tastings go, this was quite a special one, looking at 20 years of New Zealand star winery
content:
Website: https://kumeuriver.co.nz/

As tastings go, this was quite a special one, looking at 20 years of New Zealand star winery Kumeu River’s Hunting Hill Chardonnay. Paul Brajkovich was in town, representing the family, and the tasting was hosted at Farr Vintners by Stephen Browett, who first visited Kumeu in January 1990 and describes himself as ‘the world’s biggest Kumeu River fan’. Farr has imported every vintage since the 1989.

This was a tasting of every vintage made of this wine. The vineyard produces one of three single vineyard Chardonnays made by Kumeu each year in West Auckland (they’ve recently added Rays Road in Hawke’s Bay to this roster), along with Coddington and Maté’s. The 3.7 hectare site was first planted in 1981 and 1982, and the original plantings were Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon and Sauvignon Blanc. They removed the Cabernet Sauvignon quickly. The Mendoza clone Chardonnay was getting virused, so in 2001 they replanted the whole vineyard to Chardonnay, and all clone 15. The first release of Hunting Hill as a single-vineyard Chardonnay was 2006. Prior to this the old Mendoza clone Chardonnay had been a component of the estate Chardonnay.

The vineyard sits above Maté’s vineyard. The Brajkovich family bought the land in the mid-to-late 1960s, and for quite a while it was just farmland where they hunted rabbits, hence the name. It’s unlike any of the other Kumeu vineyards, in that the aspect changes quite a bit: one end faces north, then another part faces southwest.

Winemaking is nothing out of the ordinary. The hand-picked grapes are whole-bunch pressed and the juice is settled overnight. Juice yield is usually around 750 litres per tonnne, which is pretty good. Then the juice goes to a tank with the fine juice lees, and the juice is stirred to distribute them evenly as it goes to barrel. The barrels are all French oak, all from François Frères, with 25% of them new, except for 2023 and 2010, when none were new. Wild yeast fermentation with 100% malolactic. The wine stays on yeast lees until January (so almost a year in barrel), then goes to tank with fine lees for four months until bottling in May.

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2025 Kumeu, New Zealand
This was a fabulous vintage, with a long, dry summer. The hottest day was 28 C, and the fruit was very clean. Concentrated, fine, delicate and linear with a subtle mealy edge to the pristine citrus fruit. Primary and youthful, with some juiciness and great poise. Crystalline and fine. 95/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2024 Kumeu, New Zealand
Another long, dry summer but inclement weather around flowering reduced crops by around 30%. Some depth and concentration here with fine citrus fruit, lovely precision, and subtle peach and pineapple notes. Fine spices, toast and mealy notes. Real finesse, purity and intensity here. 96/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2023 Kumeu, New Zealand
Paul Brajkovich says he would like not to have this vintage again. They experienced some flooding in the winery and this was followed up by cyclone Gabriel. By this stage there were few leaves left on the vines and they picked the fruit before full ripeness. This is stony and bright and quite delicate, showing freshness and a hint of pear, as well as linear, lemony fruit. Nice purity and delicacy. A lovely wine despite the vintage. 93/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2022 Kumeu, New Zealand
A very good vintage with abundant clean fruit. Nice concentration and focus here with clean, bright lemony fruit and subtle toasty notes. Meal and pineapple, too. Refined and delicious showing great balance. 95/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2021 Kumeu, New Zealand
A frost-affected but good vintage with lower yields. Fresh, layered, stony and mineral with lovely concentrated citrus fruit and amazing poise and balanced. Crystalline with mineral complexity, as well as a touch of sour cherry on the finish. Pristine and focused. 96/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2020 Kumeu, New Zealand
This was a star vintage, perhaps the best ever, says Paul. Toast, meal, hazelnuts and spice as well as citrus on the nose. There’s some peachy richness but also linear lemony fruit with some spice and toast fringing the powerful fruit. Just beautiful. 97/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2019 Kumeu, New Zealand
Another exceptional vintage. Honey, toast and spice on the nose. Vivid and linear with lovely focus and precision as well as some richness. Notes of peach, pear and spice as well as crystalline citrus. Generous but still focused. 96/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2018 Kumeu, New Zealand
A tricky, wet vintage, but the fruit that came in was good. Taut and quite linear with nice brightness to the compact citrus fruit. Stylish and taut with good acidity. Linear. 93/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2017 Kumeu, New Zealand
This was a cooler vintage in the citrussy spectrum, with slightly lower yields. There’s a bit of development here with toast and nut complexity, as well as spice, lime and honey. Very citrussy but with lovely complexity. A touch of peachy richness on the finish. 95/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2016 Kumeu, New Zealand
An abundant, sound vintage. Wonderful aromatics. Compact lemon and peach with some fine meal and toast notes. Bold, linear and expressive with a great acid line. Beginning to show real complexity. Very fine with a tapering finish. 96/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2015 Kumeu, New Zealand
There are parallels to 2017 here: a cooler, frost-affected vintage. Chiselled, taut and linear with high acidity. Crystalline citrus fruit, a bit of toast and honey, and some peach. Real intensity here with a hint of burnt sugar. Crystalline and concentrated with high acidity. 96/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2014 Kumeu, New Zealand
This is a superstar vintage, says Paul, one of the vintages that was generous, ripe and clean. Lovely aromatics of toast and crème brulée, white peach and lemon zest. The palate has depth and concentration with nice balance. Pure and ethereal, and so well balanced. 95/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2013 Kumeu, New Zealand
A severely frost-affected vintage. They had helicopters on standby, and they flew, but there was no inversion layer of warm air so they had no effect. Normally Hunting Hill is 1500 cases; this year they got 300. But after the frost the summer was excellent. This is superb. Beautiful concentration of linear crystalline fruit, and still quite primary. There’s a touch of matchstick minerality framing the direct citrus fruit, and this still has potential for development. 97/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2012 Kumeu, New Zealand
This was a tricky year that was quite wet. Nice weight and concentration. Still youthful with peach and citrus and pineapple fruit. Lively with lovely fruit and excellent balance. Great precision to this wine with a delicate finish. 94/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2011 Kumeu, New Zealand
This was a tricky year with a wet harvest, and lots of selection was needed. Some development here: toast and peach with some pear and spice. There’s a bit of evolution with pithy structure and ripe fruit. Toasty, with a hint of marmalade. 93/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2010 Kumeu, New Zealand
This was a frost-affected vintage but a very good one. No new oak used this year. Complex nose of toast and pineapple and spice. The palate is concentrated and intense with lovely lemony detail. Very expressive with some complexity. Juicy, fine and linear with real depth and focus. Intense and fine. 96/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2009 Kumeu, New Zealand
This was a good, abundant year with clean fruit. Fine aromatics of toast, white peach and citrus. Nice weight and intensity with lovely freshness, and a tapering finish. There’s a hint of pineapple too. 95/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2008 Kumeu, New Zealand
A very warm year with a run of days over 30 C, which is unusual in Kumeu. Ripe and generous, but still chiselled, with bright lemony fruit as well as pear and peach. Nice focus and intensity here, finishing quite mineral, with some subtle toastiness. 94/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2007 Kumeu, New Zealand
Like 2015, this was a cooler year, with a good-sized harvest. Hints of mint and candlewax on the nose, which shows lovely crystalline citrus fruit. Still youthful with good balance. Pure and refined in an elegant style. 95/100

Kumeu River Hunting Hill Chardonnay 2006 Kumeu, New Zealand
This was one of those years where everything went well. A good place to begin with this single-vineyard Chardonnay. This has some colour, and notes of toast, lime and honey. Nice depth and concentration. This is beginning to evolve nicely with crystalline citrus, peach and a hint of lime oil. Concentrated and quite beautiful. 96/100

title: A mature Penfolds tasting with Yattarna, Bin 389, St Henri, Bin 707 and Grange
summary: Penfolds is one of Australia’s most important wine companies, famous for Grange (Bin 95), the red blend they have made
content:
Penfolds is one of Australia’s most important wine companies, famous for Grange (Bin 95), the red blend they have made since the 1950s, and also a growing series of Bin wines, some of which are of very high quality and which show great ageing ability. A good example of this would be Bin 389, which used to be a very affordable blend (I remember buying this for £11.99 back in the early 1990s), but which is now quite expensive, but still much cheaper than Grange. Bin 389 was a banker for the cellar, tasting good at all stages of its life. Then there was the outlier, St Henri, made without new oak and another wine that was best left in the cellar a while. One of my favourites in the range is Bin 707, a Cabernet Sauvignon, and this wine showed really well in this tasting of some back vintages hosted by London merchant Berry Bros & Rudd (their Penfolds range is here).

Penfolds Bin 144 Yattarna Chardonnay 2015
Appealing aromatics of nuts, honey and vanilla with some linear citrus fruit. Vivid with some pear and white peach richness on the palate and a nice acid line. Concentration and finesse here. 95/100

Penfolds Bin 389 Cabernet Shiraz 2018
Concentrated and quite fresh with some vanilla and dill, some meatiness and black cherries and blackcurrant. Quite expressive but still a bit tightwound, with some mint and dill on the finish. Potential here. 94/100

Penfolds Bin 389 Cabernet Shiraz 2015
Warm, spicy and harmonious with lovely sweet black cherry and blackcurrant fruit with fine-grained tannins. Lovely structure, starting to show hints of leather, spice and earth. 95/100

Penfolds Bin 389 Cabernet Shiraz 2010
Lovely concentration and weight with nicely spicy, savoury black cherry and blackberry fruit and a touch of alcoholic warmth. Nice spicy detail on the finish, evolving well. 95/100

Penfolds St Henri Shiraz 2013
Refined nose of black cherries, blackberries and dried herbs. The palate has some warmth with a nice savoury twist to the sleek black fruits, and hints of olive and leather. Stylish. 95/100

Penfolds St Henri Shiraz 2010
So refined, developing beautifully with fresh black cherry and blackcurrant fruit. Evolving really nicely. Stylish and focused, and really lovely. 96/100

Penfolds Bin 707 Cabernet Sauvignon 2008
There’s a gravelly edge to the sweet blackcurrant fruit nose, with notes of fine dried herbs and tar. The palate is refined and structured at the same time with good definition. Really lovely. 96/100

Penfolds Bin 707 Cabernet Sauvignon 2009
Perfumed, floral black cherry and blackcurrant nose. Lovely fruit here. Good concentration on the palate with broad, sweet fruit and some spicy structure. Really refined and polished, ripe and elegant. Has a core of sweet fruit. 96/100

Penfolds Bin 95 Grange 2013
Brooding, focused nose of sweet blackcurrant fruit with spicy detail. The palate is broad, concentrated and very structured with firm tannins and some development, finishing grippy. Very tight and a bit closed right now, but showing great concentration. At the moment it’s clunky and firm. 94/100

Penfolds Bin 95 Grange 2006
Savoury, spicy edge to the nose with some earth, spice and herbs. The palate is earthy and spicy with some noticeable development – more than you might expect. Some woody notes, finishing warm and spicy with grip on the finish. In an awkward place right now. 93/100

Penfolds Bin 95 Grange 2001
Earthy, spicy nose with some development. The palate has a sweet core of ripe berry fruits with good concentration, but also the earthy, spicy development that has come earlier than you might expect. Finishing firm and earthy, this is a rich, bold wine, but lacks focus. 93/100

title: Argentina Reloaded! A tasting by Paz Levinson showing the cutting edge of Argentina’s wine offering
summary: Website: https://argentinareloaded.com/eng/ This was a special masterclass presented by Paz Levinson, an Argentine sommelier who now works for Ann Sophie
content:
Website: https://argentinareloaded.com/eng/

This was a special masterclass presented by Paz Levinson, an Argentine sommelier who now works for Ann Sophie Pic in France. Paz was supported by Christina Rasmussen of Littlewine, who had recently been on an Argentina Reloaded tour. The idea behind the ‘reloaded’ term is that this is a chance to change peoples’ perceptions about Argentine wine. Argentina is associated closely with value-for-money Malbec, and also some fancy Malbec made with the help of expensive consultants who pick too late and use too much oak. But things have changed, and if you look hard you can find some exciting, compelling wines. And while Malbec is an important story, it’s not the only one.

Some facts. Argentina is an important wine country. It has just under 200 000 hectares of vines, with a significant focus on the Malbec grape: there are 47 000 hectares of this variety in the country, and while overall vineyard area is decreasing slightly, Malbec is stable. But another important story is the family of 50 or so Criolla varieties, almost all the result of crossing Listan Prieto (Criolla Chica, or Pais, or Mission) with Moscatel de Alejandria.

Mendoza is the main region, with 76% of Argentina’s vineyard area, at 140 665 hectares (40 000 hectres are Malbec). And the Cuyo area which includes Mendoza, San Juan and La Rioja makes up 94% of the country’s vineyard.

3.4% is in the Norte area, which is Salta and Juyjuy, while Patagonia down south is 1.9%.

Interestingly, half of Argentina’s vineyards are planted with parral (a pergola system). And there are lots of ungrafted vineyards, too.

Christina remarked that she was taken by the diversity of plant material, with lots of massal selection ungrafted vineyards, and also historical varieties. The Criollas, she noted, are a real gem: European Vitis vinifera heritage but born on Argentinean soil. There’s also the diversity of terroirs: elevation and latitude are helpful here.

We began with whites. Paz noted that the whites used to be made to a recipe, and they were largely boring. Now things have changed: wild yeasts and creative elevage. And with Torrontes, all the rules have been questioned and now this once monolithic variety is beginning to perform. It has a lot of potential for skin fermentation, for example.

Aside from Malbec, Grenache shows promise. There are just 63 hectares of it in Mendoza, but it could do really well here.

And for Malbec, it’s a variety that’s very sensitive to oak, and in the past this wasn’t understood. Too much of it was used, and it overwhelmed the variety.

So, here are the wines we tried, plus a few I tried after the masterclass.

Juan Pablo Michelini Altar Uco Edad Antigua Branco 2018 Mendoza, Argentina
11.6% alcohol. This is 50% Chenin Blanc (80 year old vines, pergola), 25% Chardonnay, 25% Sauvignon Blanc. The grapes are co-fermented in concrete egg and aged for three years in Stockinger foudre. Full yellow gold colour. Powerful and intense with lime, honey and straw. Concentrated and mineral with real complexity and intensity. Quite beautiful. 95/100

Riccitelli Old Vines from Patagonia Sémillon 2024 Argentina
12.5% alcohol. Vineyard planted in late 1960s on alluvial loams. Skin macerated at low temperature for 5 days then fermented and aged in foudre. Fresh, linear and chiselled with a lovely acid line under the powerful citrus fruit. There’s also some straw, honey and pear complexity. Mineral and fine. 94/100

Macollo Wines Moscatel 2025 Mendoza, Argentina
Santiago Vignoni is the winegrower behind Macollo. His family has a history of growing grapes in the East Zone of Mendoza, which is an older area making half of Argentina’s wine, with a lot of bulk production. This is from Moscatel Rosado, a distinctive variety, grown on pergola and then fermented in old barrels after a very short skin ferment (1-2 days) to finish fermentation. It’s fruity and terpenic with some grapey notes, but also some delicacy. Nicely textured with lovely balance. Dry and appealing, and delicate and fine. 93/100

Susana Balbo Signature Barrel Fermented Torrontés 2025 Mendoza, Argentina
13% alcohol. Grown from cuttings that came from Salta, cultured yeasts, new French oak. Very floral terpenic nose, which is pure and aromatic. There’s a brightness and energy on the palate with very subtle oak influence adding a spicy sheen. Nice energy here. 93/100

Bodega Chacra Sin Azufre Pinot Noir 2022 Rio Negro, Patagonia, Argentina
This is made in oak (52%), concrete (39%) and amphorae (9%), and it’s made without any added sulfites. Supple, elegant and fine with red cherry and berry fruit as well as some savoury spiciness. There’s real elegance here with a stony, savoury, mineral edge to the fruit, and it finishes slightly drying. Classy and really interesting. 94/100

Riccitelli Wines Garnacha 2025 Gualtallary, Mendoza, Argentina
12.5% alcohol. From calcareous soils at 1400 m. This is fermented infusion style in concrete (25% whole bunch), then raised in foudres. Fresh, fine and pure with brisk cherry and raspberry fruit as well as some redcurrant. Linear and pure with high acidity, a touch of reduction and youthful fruit. So pure and tightwound. 94/100

Macollo Wines Sangiovese 2025 Rivadaria, East Zone, Mendoza, Argentina
12% alcohol. 80 year old vines grown as pergola, 20% whole bunch fermentation then aged in old oak. This is juicy and bright with a stony edge to the raspberry and cherry fruit. Nicely textured, this is stylish, showing a tight savoury undercurrent. So satisfying. 93/100

Rocamadre Malbec 2025 Paraje Altamira, Uco Valley, Mendoza, Argentina
13.5% alcohol. Juanfa Suarez makes this with 30% whole bunch in concrete. It’s deeply coloured, fresh and concentrated with sweet blackberries and black cherries, showing real freshness as well as grippy structure. Pure, with detail, and unresolved in a nice way. Crunchy and fresh. 94/100

Cultor Wines La Naissance Malbec 2024 Paraje Altamira, Uco Valley, Mendoza, Argentina
14.5% alcohol. Aged in concrete and 500 litre barrels. Floral, ripe and expressive with a distinct spicy edge to the fresh berry fruits on the nose. The palate is supple, chalky and mineral with some freshness as well as ripeness and generosisty. Nice saline finish. 95/100

Zuccardi Finca Piedra Infinita Malbec 2019 Paraje Altamira, Uco Valley, Mendoza, Argentina
14% alcohol. Fresh and vivid with nice raspberry and cherry fruit. Salty, with a hint of nice reduction. Good acidity. Salty, mineral, fine and really expressive. 95/100

Cultor Wines La Prière Malbec 2024 Gualtallary, Mendoza, Argentina
14.5% alcohol. Marcelo Belmonte has made this from the famous Monasterio sub region with its high calcium carbonate soils. 20% fermented in barrel, the matured in a mix of oak and concrete egg. Brooding nose of lush black cherry and blackberry fruit. Lush, textured and bold with with real finesse on the palate. Mineral notes as well as ripe black cherry and blackberry fruit. Salty and grainy. 95/100

Ruitini Wines Single Vineyard Gualtallary Malbec 2023 Mendoza, Argentina
13.9% alcohol. 50% oak, 50% concrete. Floral aromatics, with sweet blackberry and black cherry fruit. Classic in style. The palate is ripe and lush with a hint of chocolate, sweet berries, and an appealing spicy character. Ripe but nicely balanced. 94/100

Susana Balbo Wines BenMarco Sin Limites Malbec 2023 Gualtallary, Mendoza, Argentina
14% alcohol. Classic and structured with lovely balance. Sweet black cherries and blackberry with well integrated oak. Stylish, polished and modern. 93/100

PerSe Inseperable 2022 Gualtallary, Mendoza, Argentina
14% alcohol. Infusion style with submerged cap, then matured in concrete eggs. This is from the Monasterio sub-region. So expressive, with salt and iron notes as well as black cherries, blackberries and mineral detail. Such finesse. 96/100

El Enemigo As Bravas Malbec 2017 Uco Valley, Mendoza, Argentina
13.5% alcohol. 95% Malbec, 5% Semillon (skins, co-ferment). 100% whole bunch with 80 day post-ferment maceration, then 64 months in foudres. Lush, ripe and textural with some nice spicy detail. Grippy and grainy with nice focus and some stony minerality. Good balance, with nice grip on the finish. 95/100

Noemia Malbec 2022 Río Negro, Argentina
13.5% alcohol. 1.5 hectare vineyard planted in 1932, massale selection, flood irrigated. Powerful aromatics of aniseed, cherries and red berries with nice olive and cured meat savouriness. Some spicy oak influence. Stylish. 94/100

Valle Arriba El Cateño Malbec 2023 Calchaqui Valley, Salta
14.5% alcohol. Aged in stainless steel. Concentrated, fresh and supple; salty and mineral. Nice ripe black cherry fruit. Harmonious and elegant, this is quite beautiful, with fine-grained structure and finishing with a hint of dried tomato and olive. 95/100

El Enemigo Gran Enemigo Single Vineyard Chacayes Cabernet Franc 2021 Uco Valley, Mendoza
13.5% alcohol. 85% Cabernet Franc and 15% Malbec. Fresh, supple and floral with a slight chocolatey edge to the saline black cherry and blackberry fruit. Great balance with real finesse. 95/100

Noemia A Lisa 2023 Rio Negro, Argentina
Floral and expressive with nice mineral undercurrents to the sweet blackberry and black cherry fruit. Lush but well defined with elegance and a chalky edge to the finish. 95/100

Cultor Abisal 2024 Salta, Argentina
13.6% alcohol. This comes from a vineyard at 2700 m. So floral and expressive with vivid, saline-licked cherry and raspberry fruit. Pure, expressive and mineral with lovely floral detail and good acidity. 96/100

Lagarde Guarda Malbec 2022 Mendoza, Argentina
14% alcohol. Fresh, supple and elegant with fine red cherry fruit and nice fine-grained structure. Supple and quite elegant with a twist of liquorice. Nice weight and balance. 94/100

title: Four lovely wines at Noble Rot Mayfair: Langham, Phelan Farms, Sclavos and Suertes del Marques
summary: Popped into Noble Rot Mayfair early evening yesterday and what was initially going to be just a shared bottle ended
content:
Popped into Noble Rot Mayfair early evening yesterday and what was initially going to be just a shared bottle ended up being four shared bottles. Such good wines.

Langham Culver Classic NV Dorset, England
12% alcohol. 86% from 2022, 14% reserve wine. 45% Pinot Meunier, 43% Pinot Noir, 12% Chardonnay. Just shy of two years on lees and bottled with a dosage of 1.5 g/litre. Salty and mineral with pear and peach as well as crystalline citrus fruit and some ripe cherry. Such precision here. Rich but with focus. So delicious. 93/100

Sclavos Vino Di Sasso Robola of Cephalonia 2024 Greece
13% alcohol. Complex, textured and mineral. Bold pear and citrus with some apple and a nice saltiness as well as some wax. Subtle oily characters too. So lovely. 94/100 

Phelan Farms Pinot Noir 2024 SLO Coast, California
12.5% alcohol. From Raj Parr in Cambria. 100% whole cluster, matured in used oak. Textural and really fine with red cherries, black cherries and spice. Nicely structured with amazing floral aromatics and then wild strawberry, spice, nice tannins and sappy, grainy detail. This is quite special. 96/100 

Suertes de Marqués 7 Fuentes Listán Negro 2021 Valle de la Orotava, Tenerife
From 25 parcels around Orotava. Fine reductive hints with cranberry and raspberry as well as sweet strawberry notes. Juicy and focused with lovely tension and elegance, such focus. Grown up and profound. 95/100

title: Viña González Bastías, Maule Valley, Chile: exciting naturally made wines from an amazing old vineyard
summary: Website: https://www.vinosgonzalezbastias.com/ Jose Luís Bastías and Daniela Lorenzo are custodians of a remarkable six-hectare vineyard in Chile’s Maule Valley planted
content:
Website: https://www.vinosgonzalezbastias.com/

Jose Luís Bastías and Daniela Lorenzo are custodians of a remarkable six-hectare vineyard in Chile’s Maule Valley planted in the early 19th century. I visited on a cool day in November, and was amazed by what I saw. This vineyard is unlike any other that I’ve visited, with 200 year old bush vines taller than me.

Jose Luís is fifth generation of this family operation. He met Daniela, who is an agronomist, on a trip to Santiago. The chemistry must have been strong, as he convinced her to leave the city and head to the countryside.

Twenty kilometres away, three rivers converge on their way to the sea: the Maule, the Claro and the Loncamilla. In 2023 they flooded, and the vineyard was underwater. But it bounced back and looks very happy now. You can still find mud from the flooding in the trunks of some of the vines. Jose says that these floods, which happen every 20 years or so, are actually helping the vineyard, bringing new nutrients.

Most of the older vines, some well over 200 years old, are País. But there are also some younger Moscatel Negra vines, as well as Semillon and Torontel.

Winemaking is quite natural. For destemming, a traditional wooden Zaranda de Coligüe is used (a sheet of bamboo with the grapes caught between the gaps), and fermentation is with no additions in concrete. Then maturation takes place in amphora or traditional foudres made from Raulí oak. The only addition is a small amount of sulfites before bottling.

As well as walking the vineyard, we rowed over the river to the railway station, which is where the name for the wine project comes from.

Viña González Bastías Terre Madre 2020 Maule Valley, Chile
13% alcohol. Semillon/Torontel coferment. Grainy and supple with nice fresh citrus fruit, a hint of table grape and some nice bright acidity. There’s some structure here and also some volume in the mouth. 93/100

Viña González Bastías Naranjo 2022 Maule Valley, Chile
13% alcohol. Moscatel Rosada, Torontel and País, 60 days on skins. Cloudy yellow colour. Lovely aromatics with a hint of mint, some apricot and some pear. Fresh, nicely weighted palate with a bit of structure. So juicy and fine with a nice bright finish. So expressive. 94/100

Viña González Bastías Descabezedo 2024 Maule Valley, Chile
12.8% alcohol. This is País Rojo with 3 days on skins. Pale pink/red colour, this is juicy with a bit of grip. Nice tannins, sweet cherries, raspberries and a touch of cranberry. Very focused with lovely acid and energy. Juicy with hints of marmalade and lemon peel. 94/100

Viña González Bastías Salvaje 2023 Maule Valley, Chile
Cabernet Franc. This is fresh and vivid with black cherries and a floral, chalky edge. Pure vivid fruit with some blackcurrant and black cherry notes. Bright, structured, fruit driven and floral. 95/100

Viña González Bastías Matorral 2020 Maule Valley, Chile
13% alcohol. 100% País, raised in Rauli fudres, from 200 year old vines. This is vivid and juicy with nice redcurrant fruit and good acidity. So fresh and fine, this is pale red in colour but has lots of flavour. 95/100

Viña González Bastías Viognier Amarillo 2023 Maule Valley, Chile
Grapes are purchased from Cauquenes for this wine. 90 days on skins in stainless steel with some flor. Salty, mineral and saline with some apple and pear, and a touch of apricot. Structured and slightly oxidative, this is tangy and detailed. 95/100

Older notes

Viña González Bastías Naranjo 2019 Maule Valley, Chile
12.5% alcohol. 40% Pink Moscatel, 40% Torontel, 20% País. From 4 hectares of 200 year old bush vines. This is a cloudy golden colour. It has lovely rich flavours of peach and table grapes with some orange peel notes, some tinned pear and a twist of grapefruit, as well as a bit of pithiness. There’s a lovely texture here with subtle bitterness on the finish and a bit of structure, which counters the sweet fruit nicely. This is a really lovely orange wine. 92/100

Viña González Bastías Matorral 2019 Maule, Chile
13% alcohol. This is from Pais (aka Mission, Listan Prieto, Chileno, Hussa). From four hectares of 200 year old vines. It’s naturally made, and matured for 12 months in refurbished Chilean Raulí foudres. A very expressive lighter-styled red with red cherries, spice, some silkiness, with real purity and finesse. There’s massive drinkability here, but there’s also some seriousness: fine spices, a bit of grip, some nice mineral hints, too. It’s so enjoyable on a number of levels. 93/100

Viña González Bastías Tierra Madre 2019 Maule Valley, Chile
12.5% alcohol. 50% Semillon, 50% Torontel. This is so fine and fresh with lovely notes of mint, dried herbs and lemon. It’s a focused, fruity wine with lovely precision and delicate citrus, as well as some white peach and table grape. Fine and focused with a real brightness, and also some grainy, mineral spiciness. 92/100

title: Sicus: distinctive low-intervention wines from Catalunya
summary: Website: https://www.dynamicvines.com/producers/sicus I popped into Dynamic Vines in Bermondsey on a Saturday morning and they were showing the wines of
content:
Website: https://www.dynamicvines.com/producers/sicus

I popped into Dynamic Vines in Bermondsey on a Saturday morning and they were showing the wines of Sicus, an interesting winery based in Bonastre (near Tarrgona in Catalunya, Spain). It’s the project of Eduard Piè.

His focus is on indigenous varieties, organically grown and fermented in amphora (tinajas) made from local clay. Some of these are actually buried in the vineyards. Farming is organic, and the vineyards are no-till. Soils are limestone, and the vines are dry grown.

Sicus Pétillant Naturel A Wine Work Orange (S) 2021
Lively, tangy, bright with some savoury detail. Grippy and phenolic. Quite distinctive and delicious. Wild and structured gently fizzy. 90/100

Sicus Cartoixà Brisat (Orange) 2019
Xarel.lo is the grape variety here. This is bold, fresh, distinctive. Stony edge to the lively citrus fruit. Some orange peel. Bright and tangy with real energy. 94/100

Sicus Sumoi 2021
Single vineyard called ‘El Roldonar’, located at 185m high with a strong maritime influence. Silty soil of calcareous nature. Old vines. Whole bunch fermentation. 3 months in amphora, 5 months stainless steel. Nicely textured, some structure with good acidity too. Some warmth and texture to the cherry fruit. Just 10% alcohol. Nice savoury twist. Very distinctive with a drying finish. 93/100

Sicus Garrut 2019
Single vineyard called ‘La Obaga Del Gojo’, located at 220m with a strong maritime influence. Whole bunch. 2 months in amphora, 6 months in stainless steel. Rich, concentrated, savoury and intense with some grippy structure. Brooding and bold with firm tannins. Very gastronomic. Some texture and warmth. 92/100
